questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The weather and being close to the sea. I wanted to surf.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The best thing I have done for myself in relation to my studies.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Not that easy. But it worked out. I just needed to be patient.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was a welcome session on the first day of school.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: The woman in charge of the exchange students was unfortunately not easy to get in touch with - it wasn't until later that we were told she was sick.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was really hard, actually. If you have the opportunity wait until you are there so you can visit the different apartments and make sure that you are not getting scammed. A lot of my friends used websites such as Idealista. But watch out. Facebook is also an opportunity but again be aware.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
Look up the neighbourhood - some can be quite sketchy. I would reccomend Sa Bento or Santos. Or just to find a place near a metro - find the map on google and compare;)

And I would reccomend not living too close to the school - find something in the city.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
Remember, it is not life or death. I changed apartments during the first month. It was a bit chaotic and frustrating, but everything turned out better in the end. 

A lot of the people i know had some troubles with their apartments either with the conditions or the landlord - the standards are not the same as in Denmark. But you will be fine.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I recieved an e-mail about where and when I was supposed to show up at school. We recieved a student card at the first day.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Did not need it.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: The courses available for my semester were not quite the same as those I had chosen for my pre-approval. I feel like everyone had to change something at least once. I was lucky and got enrolled in all the classes that I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Do not stress. It is the southern of Europe so they are very chill. It will take some time but it will work out.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The courses are small (between 3-6 ECTS), so there was not a lot to study.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was different. I had to participate more than at UCPH. Also, most of the teachers took attendance. But it varies from the professors.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
International Criminal Law
EU Asylum and Migration Law
European Fundamental and Human Rights Law
International Arbitration
International Law of the Sea
Introduction to EU Competition Law
Introduction to EU Internal Market
Introduction to Islamic Legal Thought

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
EU Asylum and Migration Law - the teacher was nice, the course was relevant, and the exam was easy/doable.
European Fundamental and Human Rights Law - a passionate teacher, which made it more fun - the exam was a mood court.
International Arbitration - very intelligent teacher and the exam was easy:)
Introduction to Islamic Legal Thought - very nice teacher, interesting subject - no one ever failed this course.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Transportation is free in Lisbon if you are under 24 y/o. I paid 40 Euros for my navegante card each month.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: The rent is quite high. Food is cheap.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: You can join the clubs at the university or find your hobbies elsewhere.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Women volleyball
Male football

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Try the samba. Go to the Erasmus events at least once - then you have tried it.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Go to Nazare and see the waves.
Go surfing in Costa de Caparica.
Go watch a football match. 
A five days trip to Madeira!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Haven't met that many Portuguese but a lot of international students which waas fun.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join the other students when they are doing something.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer:
The Italians have a different approach to what it means to arrive on time - they are often late.

The language barrier can be challenging, but I think you'll just have to get used to that.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The slow life. Don't stress too much about everything. It will all work out in the end.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Be patient; they will probably not reply as fast as you want them to.
2. Choose the courses that start early in the semester. We all became friends because we met within the first weeks - I know other people who did not have those courses found it harder to make friends at school. 
3. Be open-minded. They do it differently from UCPH, but it is a nice perspective.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: You don't use books. So leave the highlighters, pencils and your reading stand at home :)

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The friendships I made.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Establishing a new life in a new country.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer:
If you are in doubt, you should just do it. You will learn so much.
 And if you don't like it, you are not that far from home, and the semester will end at some point.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
